mainTopic: Arranging the two logs as an עבודה תמה, when a service gets a פייס, and the opening of the new chapter on checking for dawn and the כהן גדול's immersion
overview: The גמרא first tests רבי זירא's equation that a service followed by another service is not one a זר is חייב מיתה for. It answers the challenges from אברים ופדרים and from תרומת הדשן, so רבי זירא's question on רבי יוחנן stands. It then revises רבי יוחנן's statement: a זר who arranges the two logs is liable because it is an עבודה תמה. רבא objects that such a service should have its own פייס. The גמרא answers that the logs were joined to the תרומת הדשן lottery for the reason given earlier in the chapter. It then tests the rule behind רבא's objection against שחיטה, the night burning of אברים ופדרים, and תרומת הדשן, and explains each case. An attempted proof from a משנה that arranging the logs is a night service is rejected. The chapter בראשונה ends. The new chapter opens with a משנה about checking for daybreak before slaughtering the תמיד, the moonlight mistake behind that check, and the rule for when a כהן needs טבילה or only קידוש ידים ורגלים.

steps.title: Challenge from burning the limbs and fats at night
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבי זירא's principle by citing the burning of אברים ופדרים, which is done at night.
steps.simpleTranslation: But what about the limbs and the fats?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי זירא's principle that a service followed by another service (not an עבודה תמה) is not one a זר is חייב מיתה for. It points to the burning of the limbs and fats, which happens at night.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Burning the אברים ופדרים can continue all night on the מזבח. A זר is חייב מיתה for it. If another service is considered to follow it, that would break רבי זירא's equation.

keyTerms.meaning: Limbs of the קרבן burned on the מזבח
Fats of the קרבן burned on the מזבח
But look at…; introduces a counter-example

phrases.english: But there are the limbs and the fats!
phrases.notes: These are burned on the altar at night.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the discussion of רבי זירא's challenge to רבי יוחנן from the previous section of the daf.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי זירא's principle about nighttime services
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A service done at night (burning limbs) seems to be a real service, which contradicts the principle.

steps.title: Burning the limbs belongs to the end of the day's service
steps.stepSummary: Burning the אברים ופדרים is really the tail end of the daytime service, not an independent nighttime service.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is the end of the daytime service.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that burning limbs at night is not truly a nighttime service. It is the finishing of the previous day's service.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The קרבנות were brought during the day, and the burning at night only completes them. So it belongs to the day and is no counter-example.

keyTerms.meaning: The end of the service
Of the daytime (Aramaic)

phrases.english: It is the end of the daytime service.
phrases.notes: It's just finishing off the previous day's work, so it doesn't count as its own night service.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 1.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reclassification: the night act is attached to the previous day's service.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Burning limbs at night is an independent nighttime service.
steps.terutzMaskana: It is the completion of the daytime service.

steps.title: Challenge from removing the ashes at night
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a second nighttime service, תרומת הדשן, as a challenge.
steps.simpleTranslation: But what about the removal of the ashes?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries a second counter-example: תרומת הדשן, removing a portion of ashes from the מזבח, which is done before dawn.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Unlike the limbs, תרומת הדשן does not finish yesterday's service. It seems to be a real service done at night, which again challenges the principle.

keyTerms.meaning: Removing a shovelful of ashes from the מזבח, the first service of the morning

phrases.english: But there is the removal of the ashes!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new counter-example, after step 2 deflected the first.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי זירא's principle about nighttime services
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: תרומת הדשן is a real service done at night and cannot be called the end of yesterday's service.

steps.title: Removing the ashes is the start of the day's service
steps.stepSummary: תרומת הדשן counts as the beginning of the daytime service, proven by רבי יוחנן's ruling about washing hands.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is the start of the daytime service. As רבי יוחנן said: if a כהן washed his hands for תרומת הדשן, he does not need to wash again the next morning, because he already washed at the start of the service.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that תרומת הדשן belongs to the next day's service, as its opening act. It proves this from רבי יוחנן's ruling about קידוש ידים ורגלים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the washing done at night for תרומת הדשן covers the whole next day, the night act and the day's service are one unit. So תרומת הדשן is attached to the day and is not a counter-example.

keyTerms.meaning: The start of the service
Washed his hands (and feet) from the כיור before serving
The next day, meaning after daybreak

steps.whyThisMatters: רבי יוחנן's ruling shows that the day's service starts before dawn with תרומת הדשן. That matters both for washing and for defining what counts as a nighttime service.

phrases.english: It is the start of the daytime service,
as Rabbi Yochanan said:
If he sanctified his hands for the removal of the ashes,
the next day he does not need to sanctify again,
for he already sanctified at the start of the service.

steps.triggerLanguage: תְּחִילַּת עֲבוֹדָה דִימָמָא הִיא, דְּאָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 3.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reclassification, supported by a proof from רבי יוחנן.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: תרומת הדשן is an independent nighttime service.
steps.terutzMaskana: It is the opening act of the daytime service.

steps.title: The difficulty against רבי יוחנן remains
steps.stepSummary: Since רבי זירא's principle survives both challenges, his question on רבי יוחנן stands.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, it is a difficulty.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא concludes that רבי זירא's principle holds. So his question against רבי יוחנן's ruling, that a זר is liable for arranging the logs, still stands. The next step resolves it by revising how רבי יוחנן's statement was reported.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both counter-examples were tied to the daytime service, so the principle stands. Arranging the logs is a nighttime act, and that makes רבי יוחנן's ruling of liability problematic. This sets up the next move: a revision of רבי יוחנן's statement.

keyTerms.meaning: If so, it remains difficult

phrases.english: If so, it is difficult!
phrases.notes: The question against רבי יוחנן stands.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Sums up the result of steps 1 through 4.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רבי זירא's principle stands, so רבי יוחנן's statement as originally reported is difficult.

steps.title: Revised version of רבי יוחנן's statement
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן's statement is reworded: a זר who arranges the two logs is liable because it is an עבודה תמה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, if it was said, this is how it was said: רבי אסי said in the name of רבי יוחנן: a זר who arranged the two logs is liable, since it is a complete service.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא fixes the problem by saying רבי יוחנן's statement was reported differently. In this version, he holds that arranging the logs is a complete service, so a זר is liable.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The revised version gives a reason for the liability: the act stands on its own and is not merely a step toward a later service. Burning the limbs afterward is a separate act, not the completion of arranging the logs.

keyTerms.meaning: If it was said, this is how it was said; a formula for revising a reported statement
A non-כהן
The two logs placed on the מזבח
A complete service, after which nothing else is needed to finish it

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the גמרא is simply dropping רבי יוחנן's ruling. The liability of the זר stays the same. What changes is the reason: arranging the logs is now called an עבודה תמה.
steps.whatToRemember: Final version: a זר who arranges the two logs is חייב מיתה because it is an עבודה תמה.

phrases.english: Rather: if it was stated, this is how it was stated:

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי אַסִּי אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: Rabbi Asi said in the name of Rabbi Yochanan:
A non-priest who arranged the two logs —
is liable, since it is a complete service.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the difficulty stated in step 5 by revising the source.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Revision of how the statement was reported
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי יוחנן's ruling conflicts with רבי זירא's principle.
steps.terutzMaskana: Arranging the logs is an עבודה תמה, so the זר is liable.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A זר who arranges the two logs is liable because it is an עבודה תמה.

steps.title: רבא: then it should need a lottery
steps.stepSummary: רבא objects that if arranging the logs is an important complete service, it should require a פייס.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא objected: if so, it should require a lottery!
steps.whatsHappening: רבא attacks the revised version. If arranging the logs is a full service, the כהנים should have drawn lots for it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Important services in the מקדש were assigned by פייס. Calling the logs an עבודה תמה makes it important, so רבא expects a פייס for it.

keyTerms.meaning: He strongly objected to it
But if so, from now on
The lottery used to assign services among the כהנים

phrases.english: Rava strongly objected to it:
But if so, it should require a lottery!

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְקֵיף לַהּ רָבָא: אֶלָּא מֵעַתָּה תִּבְעֵי פַּיִיס
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the revised statement of step 6.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that arranging the logs is an עבודה תמה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A complete, important service should be assigned by its own פייס.

steps.title: But there already is a lottery for the logs
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא questions רבא, citing a ברייתא that the winner of תרומת הדשן also arranges the logs.
steps.simpleTranslation: Doesn't it require a lottery? But it was taught: whoever won תרומת הדשן also wins the arranging of the two logs!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is surprised by רבא, since the logs are already assigned through a lottery. It quotes a ברייתא to show this.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא shows that the logs go to the winner of the תרומת הדשן lottery. So there is a פייס involved, and רבא's objection seems baseless as worded.

keyTerms.meaning: Whoever won

phrases.english: And doesn't it require a lottery?
But it was taught:
Whoever won the removal of the ashes —
shall win the arranging of the two logs!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Pushes back on רבא's objection in step 7.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: A lottery already applies to the logs, through the תרומת הדשן פייס.

steps.title: רבא meant a separate lottery
steps.stepSummary: רבא's objection is clarified: arranging the logs should get its own separate פייס.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what he meant: they should hold a lottery for it by itself!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא clarifies רבא's point. He knew about the shared lottery, but argued that a complete service deserves a lottery of its own.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Bundling the logs with תרומת הדשן suggests they are secondary. If they are an עבודה תמה, they should have their own פייס. This sharpens רבא's objection and sets up the answer.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what he meant
By itself, separately

phrases.english: This is what he meant:
They should hold a lottery for it by itself!

steps.triggerLanguage: הָכִי קָאָמַר: יְפַיְּיסוּ לָהּ בִּפְנֵי עַצְמָהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Defends רבא against step 8 by reinterpreting his words.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבא claimed there was no lottery at all.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבא claimed there should be a separate lottery.

steps.title: Answer: as we explained earlier
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers רבא by referring back to the reason given earlier in the chapter for joining the logs to תרומת הדשן.
steps.simpleTranslation: As we said.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers רבא by pointing back to an explanation given earlier in the פרק. That explanation is why the logs were attached to the תרומת הדשן lottery.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רבינו חננאל, the logs were added to the תרומת הדשן lottery as an incentive for כהנים to wake up early. The lack of a separate פייס reflects that practical arrangement. It does not show that arranging the logs is unimportant, so it can still be an עבודה תמה.

keyTerms.meaning: As we said (earlier)

steps.whatToRemember: Arranging the two logs is an עבודה תמה, so a זר is liable. It has no separate פייס only for the practical reason given earlier in the chapter.

phrases.english: As we said.
phrases.notes: This points back to the explanation given earlier in the chapter for combining the two services.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבא's clarified objection from step 9.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A complete service must have its own separate פייס.
steps.terutzMaskana: The logs share the תרומת הדשן פייס for the practical reason given earlier, without lowering their status as an עבודה תמה.

steps.title: Does Lottery Depend on Death Penalty for a Non-Priest? What About Slaughtering
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether רבא really means that only a service a זר is חייב מיתה for needs a פייס. It challenges this from שחיטה, which a זר may do, yet it has a פייס.
steps.simpleTranslation: Does this mean that a complete service, for which a non-priest is liable to death, needs a lottery, and a service a non-priest is not liable to death for does not need a lottery? But look at slaughtering!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא takes the rule hidden inside רבא's objection and tests it against a case that seems to break it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא implied that the death penalty for a זר is what makes a service important enough for a פייס. But a זר is allowed to do שחיטה, so he gets no death penalty for it. Even so, שחיטה of the תמיד was given out by פייס, which seems to contradict the rule.

keyTerms.meaning: Is that to say? (introduces a challenge to an implied rule)
a complete or important service
a non-כהן
the lottery used to assign Temple services
slaughtering, which is valid even when done by a זר

steps.confusionAlert: שחיטה is a real עבודה, but a זר doing it is not liable. That is exactly why it challenges the 'death penalty' rule.

phrases.english: Is that to say that a complete service
for which a non-priest is liable to death
requires a lottery
but if a non-priest is not liable to death for it
it does not require a lottery?
But there is slaughtering!

steps.triggerLanguage: לְמֵימְרָא דַּעֲבוֹדָה תַּמָּה וְזָר חַיָּיב עָלֶיהָ מִיתָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests the criterion behind רבא's objection after it was clarified in steps 9-10.
steps.kashyaTarget: The implied rule that a פייס is needed only for a service where a זר is חייב מיתה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: שחיטה carries no death penalty for a זר, yet it has a פייס, so the rule fails.

steps.title: Slaughtering Is the Start of the Day's Service
steps.stepSummary: שחיטה is an exception because it opens the daytime service. That special status earns it a פייס.
steps.simpleTranslation: Slaughtering is different, because it is the beginning of the daytime service.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by giving שחיטה its own separate reason for having a lottery.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule (death penalty for a זר means a פייס) stays in place. שחיטה gets a פייס for a different reason: it is the first service of the day, and that gives it extra importance.

keyTerms.meaning: it is different
the beginning of the service
of the daytime

phrases.english: Slaughtering is different
for it is the beginning of the daytime service

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא from שחיטה.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinction: the exception rests on a separate reason
steps.terutzMaskana: שחיטה gets a פייס because it begins the daytime service, so the criterion still holds.

steps.title: Does Lottery Depend on a Service Being Final? What About Limbs and Fats
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא tests a second version of the rule: a complete service (nothing comes after it) needs a פייס. It challenges this from the burning of אברים ופדרים.
steps.simpleTranslation: Does this mean that a complete service needs a lottery, and a service that has another service after it does not need a lottery? But look at the limbs and fats!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tests a second way of understanding 'complete service': a service that is not followed by another one. It brings a case that seems to break this rule too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here 'complete' means a stand-alone service that is not followed by a later service. The burning of אברים ופדרים at night has nothing after it, so it is an עבודה תמה. Yet no פייס was held for it. So the 'complete service' rule seems to fail.

keyTerms.meaning: a service followed by another service
the limbs of the offering, burned on the מזבח
the fats burned on the מזבח

phrases.english: Is that to say that a complete service
requires a lottery
whereas a service that has another service after it
does not require a lottery?
But there are the limbs and fats!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Parallel challenge, now against the 'complete service' side of רבא's reasoning.
steps.kashyaTarget: The implied rule that only a stand-alone, complete service needs a פייס
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The night burning of אברים ופדרים is a complete service with nothing after it, yet it has no פייס of its own.

steps.title: Limbs and Fats End the Day's Service
steps.stepSummary: The night burning of אברים ופדרים needs no separate פייס, because it is only the end of the daytime service.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is the end of the daytime service.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the night burning of limbs and fats is not a new, independent service. It is the tail end of the daytime service, so it needs no פייס of its own.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The burning at night only finishes the קרבנות of the previous day, so it is part of that day's service and not a stand-alone service. Because it is not an independent עבודה תמה, it does not need its own פייס, and the general rule stays in place.

keyTerms.meaning: the end of the service

phrases.english: It is the end of the daytime service

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא from אברים ופדרים by attaching the night burning to the daytime service.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinction: the exception rests on a separate reason
steps.terutzHavaAmina: אברים ופדרים disprove the 'complete service' rule.
steps.terutzMaskana: The night burning is the end of the daytime service, not an independent service, so it needs no separate פייס.

steps.title: What About Removing the Ashes
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings another case that does not fit the rule: תרומת הדשן, which also had a פייס.
steps.simpleTranslation: But there is the removal of the ashes?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises one more case that seems to break the rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: תרומת הדשן is followed by more services, so it is not an עבודה תמה. By the rule, it should not need a פייס. Yet it had its own פייס, which seems to break the rule from the other direction.

keyTerms.meaning: removing a scoop of ashes from the מזבח each morning

phrases.english: But there is the removal of the ashes?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A further counter-example after the 'end of day' answer.
steps.kashyaTarget: The implied rule that a service followed by another service does not need a פייס
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: תרומת הדשן is a service followed by other services, which by the rule needs no פייס, yet it had one.

steps.title: The Ash Lottery Came From a Past Incident
steps.stepSummary: The פייס for תרומת הדשן was set up only because of an incident in which כהנים were endangered.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because of the incident that happened.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains that the lottery for the ashes did not come from the service's importance. It came from a specific past event.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier in the פרק, כהנים raced up the ramp to win תרומת הדשן, and one was pushed and injured. Because of that danger, a פייס was introduced. This was a practical safety measure, not a sign of the service's importance, so it does not disprove the rule.

keyTerms.meaning: an incident that occurred

steps.whatToRemember: Under the rule tested from רבא's objection, a complete service where a זר is חייב מיתה needs a פייס. שחיטה gets one because it begins the day's service. The night burning of אברים ופדרים needs none, since it is only the end of the day's service. תרומת הדשן has one only because of a past incident.

phrases.english: Because of the incident that occurred

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא from תרומת הדשן and closes this testing cycle.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Historical reason: a rabbinic enactment caused by an event
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The פייס for תרומת הדשן shows that the rule is wrong.
steps.terutzMaskana: That פייס exists only because of the dangerous incident, so the rule stands.

steps.title: Proof That Arranging the Logs Is a Night Service
steps.stepSummary: מר זוטרא (or רב אשי) brings a proof from a משנה that arranging the logs may be done at night. This supports the view that it is a complete service on its own.
steps.simpleTranslation: מר זוטרא, and some say רב אשי, said: We also learned this in a משנה: The appointed one said to them, 'Go out and see if the time for slaughtering has arrived.' But it does not say 'the time for arranging the logs.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a משנה to support רבי יוחנן's view that arranging the logs is a complete service.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Arranging the logs counts as complete only if it is a night service, separate from the daytime burning of the limbs. The משנה has the כהנים check whether daybreak has come only for שחיטה, not for the logs. This suggests the logs could already be arranged at night.

keyTerms.meaning: we too have learned it (introduces a supporting source)
the official in charge
arranging the logs on the מזבח
it does not teach

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר מָר זוּטְרָא וְאִיתֵּימָא רַב אָשֵׁי
phrases.english: Mar Zutra said, and some say Rav Ashi
We too have learned it
The appointed official said to them

phrases.aramaic: צְאוּ וּרְאוּ אִם הִגִּיעַ זְמַן הַשְּׁחִיטָה
phrases.english: Go out and see if the time for slaughtering has arrived
whereas 'the time for arranging the logs'
it does not teach

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to רבי יוחנן's claim from step 6 and supports it from a משנה.
steps.raayaObject: Arranging the logs is a night service, and therefore a complete service on its own
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה 'צאו וראו אם הגיע זמן השחיטה', which mentions only שחיטה

steps.title: The משנה Mentions Only What Cannot Be Fixed
steps.stepSummary: The proof is rejected. The משנה mentions שחיטה because a mistake there cannot be fixed. A mistake with the logs can be fixed, so the משנה had no need to mention them.
steps.simpleTranslation: It teaches the one that has no fix. It does not teach the one that has a fix.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא knocks down the proof by giving another reason why the משנה mentions only שחיטה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If שחיטה is done before daybreak, the offering is ruined for good, so checking the time is critical. If the logs are arranged too early, they can simply be taken down and arranged again. So the משנה's silence about the logs does not prove they belong to the night. They may still be a day service.

keyTerms.meaning: a way to fix or correct
that one

steps.confusionAlert: The דחיה does not prove that the logs are a day service. It only shows that the משנה gives no proof either way.
steps.whatToRemember: The attempted proof fails. The משנה names only the service that cannot be fixed if done too early, so the timing of arranging the logs is still unproven.

phrases.english: That which has no remedy, it teaches

phrases.aramaic: הָךְ דְּאִית לַהּ תַּקַּנְתָּא — לָא קָתָנֵי
phrases.english: that which has a remedy, it does not teach

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the ראיה of step 17.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the proof, not רבי יוחנן's position
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The משנה's silence about the logs has another explanation: arranging them early can be fixed, while early שחיטה cannot.

steps.title: Hadran — Closing the chapter בראשונה
steps.stepSummary: The closing formula marking the end of the chapter בראשונה.
steps.simpleTranslation: We will return to you, chapter בראשונה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא marks the end of the chapter called בראשונה. A new chapter is about to begin.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The הדרן line is not part of the argument. It is a farewell to the chapter and a promise to come back and learn it again. The previous discussion about פייסות and the order of the עבודה is now closed.

keyTerms.meaning: We will return to you (a closing formula for a chapter)
'At first': the name of the chapter being closed

steps.whatToRemember: The chapter בראשונה, which dealt with the פייסות and the early morning order of the עבודה, ends here. A new chapter begins with the next line.

phrases.english: We will return to you, [chapter] 'At first'
phrases.notes: This is the traditional line said when finishing a chapter.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the chapter after the final דחיה about arranging the logs.

steps.title: Checking whether it is time to slaughter
steps.stepSummary: The ממונה sends כהנים to check for daybreak. If day has come, the watcher calls out 'ברקאי'.
steps.simpleTranslation: The appointed one said to them: Go out and see whether the time for slaughtering has arrived. If it has arrived, the one watching says: 'ברקאי' (it is light).
steps.whatsHappening: A new chapter opens with a משנה. The ממונה sends כהנים out to check whether daylight has come, so that the תמיד can be slaughtered.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תמיד of the morning may only be slaughtered once it is day. So they did not rely on a guess. They sent someone to look, and he announced the dawn with a fixed word, 'ברקאי'.

keyTerms.meaning: The appointed official in charge of the כהנים
The time when slaughtering is allowed (daytime)
The one watching / looking out
'It is light!': the dawn has shone

phrases.english: The appointed one said to them:
Go out and see
whether the time for slaughtering has arrived.
If it has arrived, the one watching says:
'There is light!'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new chapter after the Hadran.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Before slaughtering the תמיד, a כהן must check and announce that daylight has come.

steps.title: מתיא בן שמואל's version of the check
steps.stepSummary: מתיא בן שמואל says the question was 'Has the whole east lit up as far as חברון?' and the answer was 'Yes!'
steps.simpleTranslation: מתיא בן שמואל says: The appointed one would ask, 'Has the whole eastern sky lit up, all the way to חברון?' And the watcher would say, 'Yes!'
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה brings a second version of how the dawn was announced. In this version the ממונה asks a specific question and the watcher answers 'yes'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: מתיא בן שמואל does not change the law that one must wait for daylight. He describes a different wording. In his version the light must spread across the whole eastern sky, as far as חברון, which is a clear sign of real dawn.

keyTerms.meaning: The ממונה in charge of the lots, who reports the procedure
The east (where the dawn appears)
חברון, a city south of ירושלים
Yes

phrases.english: Matya ben Shmuel says:
'Has the face of the entire east lit up
as far as Hebron?'
And he [the watcher] says: 'Yes!'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers an alternative wording for the dawn announcement in step 20.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to מתיא בן שמואל, the check was a question-and-answer about light spreading across the whole east up to חברון.

steps.title: Why was such a careful check needed?
steps.stepSummary: The משנה asks why they needed a formal check, since daylight is usually obvious.
steps.simpleTranslation: And why did they need this?
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה stops to ask a question. Why bother with a special lookout and announcement, when anyone can usually tell that it is day? This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question points out that the procedure seems unnecessary. Its purpose is to lead into the historical reason behind it.

keyTerms.meaning: They needed / it was necessary

phrases.english: And why did they need this?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the need for the procedure described in steps 20–21.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The reason a formal dawn-check was instituted.

steps.title: The moonlight mistake
steps.stepSummary: Once, moonlight was mistaken for dawn. They slaughtered the תמיד too early, and it had to be burned.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because once the light of the moon rose, and they thought the east had lit up. They slaughtered the תמיד, and it was taken out to the place of burning.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה answers its question with a story. A real mistake once happened, so they made a careful check to stop it from happening again.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Moonlight fooled the כהנים into thinking it was dawn. A תמיד slaughtered at night is פסול, so it had to be burned. This loss is why the formal check was set up.

keyTerms.meaning: The light of the moon
The daily communal offering
The place where disqualified קדשים are burned

steps.whatToRemember: The dawn-check exists because of a real mistake. A תמיד slaughtered before daylight is פסול and must be burned.

phrases.english: Because one time
the light of the moon rose,
and they thought that the east had lit up,
and they slaughtered the daily offering,
and they took it out to the place of burning.
phrases.notes: It was disqualified because it was slaughtered at night.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 22.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: An incident in which moonlight was mistaken for dawn led to a disqualified תמיד. So a careful check was instituted.

steps.title: The כהן גדול goes down to immerse
steps.stepSummary: After daybreak is confirmed, they bring the כהן גדול down to the בית הטבילה.
steps.simpleTranslation: They brought the כהן גדול down to the place of immersion.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה moves to the next stage of the day. The כהן גדול is led to immerse before starting the day's עבודה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once it is day, the כהן גדול begins his service. On יום הכיפורים, he immerses before he puts on his garments and begins the עבודה. This line starts the order of his immersions.

keyTerms.meaning: The High Priest
The place of immersion

phrases.english: They brought the High Priest down
to the place of immersion.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the order of the day once dawn has been confirmed.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: After daybreak, the כהן גדול is taken to immerse.

steps.title: Temple rule: when to immerse and when to wash
steps.stepSummary: A general Temple rule: relieving oneself requires טבילה, while urinating requires only קידוש ידים ורגלים.
steps.simpleTranslation: This was the rule in the מקדש: Anyone who 'covers his feet' (relieves himself) needs to immerse. Anyone who urinates needs to wash his hands and feet.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה pauses to state a general rule for כהנים in the מקדש. It explains which bodily acts require a full immersion and which require only washing hands and feet.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Covering the feet' is a polite way of saying relieving oneself. That act requires a full טבילה before serving again. Urinating is less serious, so it only requires קידוש ידים ורגלים from the כיור.

keyTerms.meaning: This is the general rule
'Covers his feet': a polite term for relieving oneself
Requires immersion
One who urinates
Washing hands and feet from the כיור before service

steps.confusionAlert: 'מיסך את רגליו' does not literally mean covering one's feet. It is a polite expression for relieving oneself.
steps.whatToRemember: Relieving oneself requires a full טבילה. Urinating requires only קידוש ידים ורגלים.

phrases.english: This was the rule in the Temple:
Anyone who covers his feet —
phrases.notes: A polite expression for relieving oneself.

phrases.english: requires immersion,
and anyone who urinates —
requires sanctification of hands and feet.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a general rule connected to the immersion in step 24.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Relieving oneself requires טבילה. Urinating requires only קידוש ידים ורגלים.
steps.whyThisMatters: This rule sets the standard of purity for every כהן serving in the מקדש. It explains why the כהן גדול immerses at various points during the day.
